title: 09 Kumo Kōbō: Japanese ceramics workshop hero
strengths: One object, drawn well: the tea bowl's iron glaze with ash runs, a thin foot, a soft ground shadow; the caption 'No. 214, tea bowl · Iron glaze, ash run · 11.5 × 8 cm' is how a workshop labels work
Shippori Mincho for English and Japanese with Zen Kaku Gothic for small text; the vertical phrase and the vermilion seal are quiet and placed, not sprinkled
Corner data (Autumn opening · 2 November, 01 — 06 pagination, 'Wood-fired stoneware · since 1998') and copy with facts (two potters, one kiln, three-day firings, twice a year)
slop_signals: A large soft brown blurred disc behind the bowl: a gradient blob standing in for a moon or kiln glow
Two underlined CTAs stacked ('See the autumn kiln opening ->', 'Visit the workshop') where one would do
Vertical calligraphy + red seal + washi texture is the expected 'Japanese minimal' kit; well handled, but recognisable
fixes: Remove the blurred disc, or replace it with a hard-edged ink circle (an enso) or nothing; the bowl's shadow already grounds it
One link; fold 'Visit the workshop' into the nav
Photograph or paint a second bowl state (a detail of the glaze) for the 01-06 pager so the pagination means something

references.what: Ceramic pieces photographed top-down are the whole art direction, headline small and centred, no blob behind them
Warm photograph, type that whispers in the corner; the same quiet register with a real image
One sentence, one underline, nothing else; shows that a single CTA is enough
Corner-pinned micro type (date, counter, caption) around an asymmetric headline; our corner labels follow this
